title: From UCCX and UCCE
blurb: A teaching bridge: skills, modules, modes, data, the gateway, and a go/no-go that can stop.
summary: There is no import button. Rebuild the domain, then move a number.

lessons.title: There is no import button
objectives: Call this track a teaching bridge
Start from the Five9 planning order
paragraphs: This track is a teaching bridge. Five9's public pages name Cisco as a SIP gateway type. They do not publish a wizard that reads a UCCX script or a UCCE dial plan and emits a domain.
The planning order still applies on the Five9 side: skills, users, lists, dispositions, profiles, then campaigns. A cutover that starts by 'moving the script' skips the objects the script will name.

lessons.title: CSQs, skills, and the partition you will not find
objectives: Map a CSQ to a skill group
paragraphs: In this teaching map, a UCCX contact service queue is closest to a Five9 skill group: the people who can take that work. A UCCE skill group is a similar idea with a different name. Precision queues and attributes do not have a one-field equivalent you should invent.
Five9 does not use CUCM partitions or calling search spaces. The boundary is the domain. If two businesses must not share lists, they are two domains, not two partitions.

lessons.title: Scripts are rebuilt in modules
objectives: Treat the builder export as a study file
paragraphs: A UCCX script is a document in Cisco's editor. A Five9 IVR script is a chain of modules from the IVR Administrator's Guide: Menu, Get Digits, If/Else, Skill Transfer, Play, and the rest of that chapter. The lab's builder speaks those names and exports a learning JSON that VCC will not import.
Time-of-day branches, a language prompt, and a transfer to a skill are the usual bones. Rebuild them. Do not hex-edit the old file.
uncertain: Module mapping from UCCX steps is instructional. Validate every script in a domain.

lessons.title: Dialing modes do not survive the move by osmosis
objectives: Choose a Five9 mode by its own definition
Keep the simulator in the classroom
paragraphs: UCCE outbound has its own pacing words. Five9's product pages talk about Preview, Progressive, Power, Predictive, and Manual Touch. The simulator in this lab is a classroom clock, not either vendor's algorithm.

Progressive on the outbound product page is one call per available agent. The dialer page also describes an adaptive pace and a smaller team. Quote the page you mean. Do not copy a Cisco lines-per-port number into Max Abandoned Call Percentage. This lab does not state a numeric default for that field.
uncertain: The dialer product page and the outbound product page describe progressive pacing in different words. Quote the page you use.

lessons.title: Numbers, lists, and ANI are a data project
objectives: Load lists, DNC, and dispositions as data
paragraphs: DNIS values, calling lists, dispositions, and do-not-call entries are domain data. They are not inside the Cisco script file. A cutover that moves only the IVR still has nothing to dial and nowhere legal to send a call.

Campaign profiles hold the ANI override. Local ANI is not the Certified Caller program. If the old system presented a specific caller ID, create the profile and assign it in Advanced mode, then ask separately whether attestation is in scope.

lessons.title: The gateway cut, without pretending to be the CUBE guide
objectives: Keep Five9 requirements and gateway chores in two columns
Do not cite a Cisco example as a Five9 default
paragraphs: When the third SIP story is a Cisco gateway, the technical requirements are still the Five9 side: DNS SRV preferred, G.711 as the default codec, TLS 1.2, no double NAT. What the gateway itself must rewrite — number format, a normalization script, early media — lives in Cisco's documentation.

Practitioner notes often mention G.711 at 20 ms, NANP versus E.164, and 'do not send internal extensions.' Treat every one of those as uncertain until the trunk guide you and the carrier signed actually says them. RFC 3261 tells you what an INVITE is. It does not choose your dial plan.

lessons.title: Cutover morning is a checklist, not a mood
objectives: Run one DNIS, one dial, one pop, one location
Stop the repoint when any line fails
paragraphs: The morning the numbers move, the domain should already contain skills, a script, a running inbound campaign, loaded lists, dispositions, DNC, an assigned profile, and a desktop the agent has signed into. E911 addresses have to be dispatchable for the place the agent actually is. A stale office address is not a courtesy.

Keep a backout that does not depend on a disabled Five9 domain's DIDs surviving past their retention window. Test one DNIS, one outbound record, one pop, and one 911 procedure in the lab domain before the carrier repoints the range.
